UnderstandingPrompt: Lords' party size limits represent direct changes to native size limits of each official lord party of the ruler, current owner clans of local-policy source settlements, specified clans or nationwide lords. Local-policy source or selected settlements map to their current owner clans and affect all their official lord parties. Ruler targets affect only the party personally led by the current ruler and transfer with succession. Clan targets affect all that clan's lord parties. Nationwide targets affect all current clans of the kingdom, including mercenary clans. Garrisons, militia, caravans, villagers, messengers and other non-official lord parties are unaffected. Do not interpret army formation willingness, army numbers, recruitment, garrison capacity, wages or soldier experience as party size limits.
EvaluationPrompt: value is a fixed headcount added to each affected lord party's native calculation and must be an integer from -100 to +100. +20 increases every party limit by 20; -20 reduces it by 20. Multiple policies add together; the final limit has a minimum of 1. Mild organizational changes usually use 5 to 10; regular expansion or downsizing 10 to 25; major standing-army reform 25 to 50; extreme royal-guard or total-mobilization reform 50 to 80. Reserve 80 to 100 for ruler-exclusive targets or exceptionally strong policy evidence. Nationwide effects change many lord parties and usually use 5 to 20, generally no more than 30. Assess negatives cautiously on the same scale so ordinary policies do not remove lords' basic fighting capability.
